signal_updates.headline: Schedule Policy/Career reclassification effective March 8, 2026; Second Amended Complaint filed March 4, 2026 challenging entire framework; VA union contract restored March 13, 2026 via preliminary injunction
signal_updates.summary: The Trump administration's Schedule Policy/Career reclassification (formerly Schedule F) took effect March 8, 2026, converting approximately 50,000 federal employees in policy-influencing roles from career civil service to at-will employment with reduced protections. On March 4, 2026, a coalition including AFGE, AFSCME, AFL-CIO, PEER, and Democracy Forward filed a Second Amended Complaint in the Maryland federal court case (PEER v. Trump) expanding the legal challenge to target the entire Schedule Policy/Career framework—the underlying executive order, OPM's final rule, and the broader reclassification effort. Simultaneously, on March 13, 2026, a federal judge granted a preliminary injunction ordering the Department of Veterans Affairs to reinstate AFGE's master collective bargaining agreement covering 320,000 VA employees, blocking the VA Secretary's unilateral termination of union protections.
signal_updates.analyst_note: Dominant active signal; search results confirm operationalization and litigation escalation, with private-sector transition signals amplifying leverage.
